dslr-camera.context: A digital SLR camera seen from the side, with a raised prism hump on top, a deep grip and a big lens barrel at the front. Used for photography apps, camera gear shops and photo equipment lists.

medium-format-camera.context: A boxy medium format camera with a square lens on the front and a waist level finder hood folded up on top. Used for studio portrait photography, film photography and classic camera collections.

point-and-shoot-camera.context: A slim compact camera with a small lens off to one side, a flash window and a shutter button on top. Used for casual photos, travel snapshots and simple camera categories.

disposable-camera.context: A single use film camera with a wrap band, a small fixed lens, a flash window and a wheel on top. Used for weddings, parties, travel nostalgia and retro photo themes.

box-camera.context: An old fashioned upright box camera with a small lens low on the front, a carrying handle and a winding key at the side. Used for vintage photography, history and retro design.

hand-crank-film-camera.context: An early movie camera with a hand crank on top and a round lens, standing on a tall tripod. Used for silent film, film history, cinema classics and movie production themes.

camera-film-magazine.context: A film camera with two round film magazine lobes sitting on its top like ears. Used for cinema camera equipment, film stock and motion picture production.

wide-angle-lens.context: A short lens barrel from the side with a large curved front element that bulges wider than the body. Used for landscape and architecture photography, real estate photos and lens guides.

zoom-lens.context: A long lens barrel with a wide ribbed zoom ring and small focal length marks along the back. Used for telephoto and sports photography, wildlife shooting and zoom controls.

tilt-shift-lens.context: A lens barrel whose front half is tilted on a hinge with a small adjustment knob on top. Used for architecture photography, miniature effect shots and perspective control.

anamorphic-lens.context: The front of a cinema lens with a stretched oval glass element and a thin horizontal streak across it. Used for widescreen film looks, cinematic video and lens flare effects.

pancake-lens.context: A very thin flat lens fitted to the front of a small camera body that has a little hump on top. Used for compact kits, street photography and slim mirrorless camera gear.

cine-lens.context: A cylinder shaped cinema lens with two raised gear rings around its barrel for focus and aperture. Used for film production gear, camera rentals and cinematography.

lens-mount.context: The front of a camera body showing the round mount opening with three bayonet tabs around the rim and a small locking pin. Used for lens compatibility, camera specifications and lens change guides.

extension-tube.context: A hollow tube with a wide mounting flange at each end, fitted between a camera and a lens. Used for macro and close up photography and camera accessory lists.

lens-adapter.context: A stepped ring with a wide flange on one end and a narrower mount on the other, used to join a lens to a different camera. Appears in camera gear lists and compatibility settings.

teleconverter.context: A short stubby cylinder with end mounts and a small glass element visible in its center, fitted between lens and camera. Used for extending lens reach in wildlife and sports photography.

polarizing-filter.context: A round screw on filter with an outer ring and parallel diagonal lines across its glass. Used for cutting glare and reflections and deepening skies in photography.

graduated-filter.context: A square filter plate that is dark across its top half and clear across the bottom half. Used for balancing bright skies against dark ground in landscape photography.

nd-filter.context: A round screw on filter with solid dark glass and a small glint of light on it. Used for long exposures, smooth water shots and shooting video in bright sun.

matte-box.context: A flared hood with a bellows fold and a tilted flap, mounted in front of a camera lens. Used for shading lenses and holding filters on film and video sets.

follow-focus.context: A large round focus knob with a small gear that meshes with the toothed ring of a lens. Used for smooth manual focus pulls on film and video cameras.

lens-flare.context: A bright four point star in the corner with a diagonal line of smaller circles trailing away from it. Used for light effects in photo editing, filters and cinematic looks.

lens-cleaning-pen.context: A pen shaped tool with a soft brush at one end and a round felt tip at the other, drawn on a diagonal. Used for cleaning lenses, filters and camera sensors.

chromatic-aberration.context: A circle outline drawn twice with a small offset so a thin double edge fringe shows on one side. Used for lens quality notes, photo editing corrections and optics explanations.

barrel-distortion.context: A square grid whose lines bulge outward toward the edges, like the side of a barrel. Used for lens distortion, wide angle correction and image warping controls.

field-of-view.context: A small camera on the left with two lines opening into a wide cone and an arc across the opening. Used for camera coverage, lens angle, security camera placement and game camera settings.

rack-focus.context: A solid sharp shape in front of a dashed soft shape behind it, showing focus shifting between two subjects. Used for cinematography, depth of field and video editing tools.

focus-peaking.context: A flower inside viewfinder corner marks, with its edge traced by a ring of small bright dots. Used for manual focus aids on cameras and video apps.

focus-stacking.context: A stack of offset image layers with a small flower on the front layer. Used for macro photography, merging several shots into one sharp image and photo editing.

camera-strap.context: A camera body with a wide padded strap rising from both ends and meeting above it. Used for camera accessories, carrying gear and photo shop categories.

hot-shoe.context: A close view of the top of a camera body with a flat rectangular accessory slot and a center contact dot. Used for mounting flashes, microphones and lights on a camera.

camera-mode-dial.context: A round ridged dial seen from above with small marks around its edge and a pointer line. Used for exposure mode selection, camera settings and manual control guides.

articulating-screen.context: The back of a camera with its screen swung out to the side on a hinge and tilted. Used for vlogging cameras, selfie shooting and low or high angle framing.

camera-rain-cover.context: A camera wrapped in a loose hooded sleeve with a few raindrops falling on top. Used for weather protection gear and outdoor photography in wet conditions.

camera-cage.context: A camera body enclosed by a rectangular metal frame with a handle across the top. Used for adding monitors, microphones and accessories to video cameras.

quick-release-plate.context: A flat mounting plate with a captive screw near the top and slanted dovetail edges on both sides. Used for attaching cameras quickly to tripod heads and rigs.

camera-brick-battery.context: A large rectangular brick battery with a stack of level bars and a tapered mounting plate on its base. Used for powering cinema cameras and showing battery charge on film sets.

star-test-chart.context: A square focus chart with a round star of alternating dark and light wedges meeting in the center. Used for checking lens sharpness, focus and resolution.

crop-factor.context: A large outer frame with a smaller inner frame in its corner and a small diagonal arrow pointing at the inner corner. Used for comparing sensor sizes and equivalent focal lengths.

slr-cross-section.context: A cut away view of an SLR camera showing the lens, an angled mirror inside the body and the prism leading to the viewfinder. Used for explaining how a reflex camera works.

smartphone-video-rig.context: A phone held sideways in a handled frame with a small microphone and a light mounted on top. Used for mobile filmmaking, vlogging and content creator gear.

phone-clip-lens.context: A phone with a round clip on lens sitting over its camera at the top corner. Used for macro, wide angle and fisheye add-on lenses for mobile photography.

shoulder-rig.context: A camera on a rail over a curved shoulder pad with two hand grips below. Used for handheld documentary and news shooting with a stable, comfortable camera position.

camera-stabilizer-vest.context: A body vest with a spring arm holding a camera on a vertical post that has a weight at the bottom. Used for smooth moving shots in film and sports coverage.

suction-cup-mount.context: A large round suction cup pad with a short jointed arm holding a small camera. Used for mounting cameras on cars and windows for driving and action shots.

cable-cam.context: A camera hanging from a small carriage on cables stretched between two tall posts. Used for aerial views over stadiums, concerts and sports broadcasts.

camera-car.context: A car in side view with a long arm reaching out from its roof and holding a camera in front of it. Used for chase scenes and moving shots in film production.

robotic-camera-arm.context: An industrial robot arm on a base with jointed segments holding a camera at its tip. Used for repeatable motion control shots, product videos and automated studios.

apple-box.context: A wooden box seen at an angle with a hand hole cut into its end. Used for film set grip equipment, stands, risers and sitting or standing on.

c-stand.context: A stand with three spread legs, a tall column and a side arm with a clamp at the top. Used for holding lights, flags and diffusion on film and photo sets.

copy-stand.context: A flat baseboard with an upright column holding a camera that points straight down at the board. Used for photographing documents, artwork and flat objects.

photo-turntable.context: A low round rotating platform with a small product box on top and a curved arrow beneath it. Used for 360 degree product photography and spinning displays.

star-tracker-mount.context: A tripod top with a tilted wedge mount holding a camera, pointed toward a small four point star. Used for astrophotography and long night sky exposures.

fresnel-light.context: A stage light seen from the front, with concentric stepped lens rings in a square housing and two tilted barn door flaps. Used for theatre, film and studio lighting.

ellipsoidal-spotlight.context: A long narrow spotlight barrel with a lens tube at the front, shutter handles sticking up and a yoke below. Used for sharp edged theatre lighting and gobo projection.

moving-head-light.context: A round light head resting in a U shaped yoke above a square base, with a narrow beam rising from it. Used for concert, club and event lighting that pans and tilts.

follow-spot.context: A long cylindrical spotlight on a tall stand with a handle at the back and a single narrow beam. Used for lighting a performer on stage as they move.

footlights.context: A row of small hooded lamps along the front edge of a stage floor shining upward. Used for theatre history, stage lighting and old fashioned stage looks.

lighting-console.context: A sloped control desk with a row of vertical fader sliders and a small screen above it. Used for controlling stage and event lighting cues.

lighting-plot.context: A top down stage outline with small light symbols along a bar above it. Used for lighting design plans and rigging layouts for theatre and events.

gobo.context: A round metal disc with a leaf shaped cut out, with the same leaf shape projected as light underneath. Used for patterned light effects in theatre, events and architecture.

lighting-gel.context: A stage lamp with a square colored filter sheet held in a frame at its front. Used for tinting stage and film lights and changing their color.

snoot.context: A light head with a long narrowing tube on its front that makes a small round spot of light. Used for studio photography accents and tight pools of light.

honeycomb-grid.context: A round disc filled with a hexagonal honeycomb pattern that fits over a light reflector. Used for narrowing light spread in studio photography and video lighting.

lantern-softbox.context: A round paper lantern shaped ball light hanging from the end of a long boom pole. Used for soft all around light on film sets and portrait shoots.

lighting-flag.context: A black rectangular panel on an arm clamped to a stand, used to block part of a light. Used for shaping shadows and cutting spill on film and photo sets.

butterfly-frame.context: A large square fabric frame held overhead on two tall stands with the sun and its rays above it. Used for softening harsh sunlight on outdoor film and photo shoots.

cucoloris.context: A board with irregular cut out holes held in front of a light, with a dappled pattern of light spots below it. Used for creating leafy or broken shadows in film and photography.

studio-strobe.context: A studio flash head with a flared reflector bowl and a vented back, standing on a stand. Used for portrait and product photography lighting.

flash-diffuser.context: A hot shoe flash unit with a rounded translucent dome cap over its head. Used for softening on camera flash light and for photo accessory lists.

led-light-tube.context: A slim handheld light wand standing upright with a glowing tube and rays on both sides. Used for creative video lighting, accent colors and portable light effects.

audience-blinder.context: A rectangular lamp panel with a two by two grid of round bright lamps and rays shining out of the top. Used for flooding the audience with light at concerts and shows.

blacklight.context: A long fluorescent tube in a fixture with short wavy lines radiating down from it. Used for ultraviolet lighting, glow in the dark effects and party lighting.

three-point-lighting.context: A top down diagram with a subject circle in the middle and three lamps placed around it, each with a short ray. Used for explaining key, fill and back lighting setups.

split-lighting.context: A face outline divided down the middle, with one half filled solid and the other half left open, and a small nose mark. Used for dramatic portrait lighting and shadow guides.

catchlight.context: An eye with a small square window shaped highlight reflected in the pupil. Used for portrait photography, retouching and explaining how light sources show in eyes.

color-temperature.context: A horizontal scale with a flame at the warm end, a snowflake at the cool end and a pointer underneath. Used for white balance and kelvin settings in cameras and lights.

flash-powder-lamp.context: An old handheld flash pan raised on a stick, with a bright burst above it and small puffs of smoke at its sides. Used for early photography history and vintage flash themes.

orchestra-pit.context: A stage floor with a sunken pit between its two edges, holding a small conductor with a raised baton. Used for theatre, opera, musicals and live performance venues.
